aid-ask.summary: Answers a question about your project with sources, using the Knowledge Base, the code and any work in progress.
aid-ask.when: Use it to learn how something works or where a piece of work stands. To change something, use /aid-triage or a work skill instead.
aid-ask.example: /aid-ask where is the retry logic for payments?

steps.title: Read your question
steps.text: With no question it prints usage and stops.

steps.title: Choose how deep to go
steps.text: A small question is answered from a few Knowledge Base documents or files; a broad one goes to a read-only research agent.

steps.title: Check the tracker
steps.text: If you name a ticket and a tracker connector exists, it reads that ticket too.

steps.title: Answer with sources
steps.text: The reply has an Answer part and a Sources part listing documents and file paths.

steps.title: Record a gap
steps.text: If it cannot answer, it says so, never invents, and logs the missing knowledge as a question.

writes: Nothing when it can answer. It only reads.
When it cannot answer: one new question entry in `.aid/knowledge/STATE.md`, or in the work's `STATE.yml` when the question is about that work.
notes: Each answer comes from the Knowledge Base and the code, so a missing or stale Knowledge Base gives weak answers.
It never edits Knowledge Base documents, settings or code. To close a gap it suggests /aid-update-kb.

aid-brainstorm.summary: Explore a fuzzy problem and turn it into a kept design note, without deciding anything.
aid-brainstorm.when: Use it when you do not yet have a clear question. Once it is a question, use /aid-research; once the shape is clear, use /aid-design.
aid-brainstorm.example: /aid-brainstorm how should customers manage multiple workspaces

steps.title: Intake
steps.text: Asks what you want to explore if you gave no subject. It never turns a vague subject away. Suggests a short file name for the note and asks you to confirm it.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: An architect agent explores framings, angles and prior art, using your Knowledge Base and code, then narrows to the directions worth pursuing. It writes the note.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: An independent reviewer checks the note. It is reworked until clean, or stops after 3 rounds.

steps.title: Present
steps.text: Shows the note and stops. You decide: run it again to refine, promote it, or drop it.

writes: A design note at .aid/design/<name>.md.
A work folder at .aid/works/work-NNN-<short-name>/ with STATE.yml, in its own git worktree.
Never your source code and never the Knowledge Base.
aid-brainstorm.gate: You decide what to do with the note. Nothing builds from it automatically.
notes: There is no create step that consumes this note. It stays in .aid/design/ until you act on it or delete it.

aid-chat.summary: Lets this AI coding session talk to another one: ask, answer or work alongside a peer agent.
aid-chat.when: Use it when two agent sessions, perhaps in different folders or tools, need to coordinate. It does not start or manage the chat server.
aid-chat.example: /aid-chat ask the agent named api-work about the schema

steps.title: Join
steps.text: The session registers once and gets a two-word name, such as green-giraffe, that others use to reach it.

steps.title: Find someone
steps.text: The roster shows each agent, its tool, how long it has been quiet and whether it is available.

steps.title: Open a channel
steps.text: It opens a channel and pulls in a named agent right away; it can also join one that already exists.

steps.title: Talk
steps.text: It sends messages, replies to a specific one, mentions someone, or whispers to one member.

steps.title: Handle incoming messages
steps.text: A message wakes an idle session; it says in one line what arrived, replies if needed, then acknowledges.

steps.title: Leave
steps.text: It leaves the channel; the last one out ends it and its messages are gone.

writes: Nothing in your project files. Messages go through the chat hub.
notes: A session can be in one channel at a time.
Needs the `aid chat` command and a running chat hub; the person who runs the hub starts and stops it.
It does not change chat settings or remove other agents.
The person at the session cannot see the channel, so the agent says what arrived before acting on it.

aid-config.summary: Shows your AID settings, or changes one of them, such as project name, type or minimum grade.
aid-config.when: Use it first on a new project, and any time you want to see or change a setting. It only edits the settings file, nothing else.

steps.title: Create the file if needed
steps.text: If `.aid/settings.yml` does not exist yet, it is copied in from the template.

steps.title: Show or look up
steps.text: With no key it prints every setting in a table and flags values you have not filled in; with a key it shows that one value.

steps.title: Ask for the new value
steps.text: You pick a suggestion, keep the current value, or type your own.

steps.title: Check the value
steps.text: Bad values are refused and you are asked again; for example a grade must look like A, B+ or C-.

steps.title: Save in place
steps.text: Only that one line changes and it prints the old and new value.

writes: `.aid/settings.yml` (one line, or the whole file when it is first created from the template).
aid-config.gate: You choose or type the new value for the key you asked about.
notes: The words after the skill name are settings keys, not kinds of work. Any other key is refused.
type is brownfield or greenfield; source_control is none, git, svn or mercurial; heartbeat_interval is minutes (0 turns it off).
The knowledge block in the file is written by other skills and cannot be changed here.
Does not run in Plan mode, because it writes a file.

aid-create.summary: Plan something new: code such as an API, UI or job, a project document in the Knowledge Base, or a standalone document.
aid-create.when: Use it when the thing does not exist yet. To change something that exists, use /aid-update; to settle the shape first, use /aid-design.
aid-create.example: /aid-create api a read endpoint for orders with pagination

steps.title: Pick the route
steps.text: The first word of your request can be a kind. For code kinds (and no kind) it runs the planning steps below. For the Knowledge Base and document kinds it follows its own shorter path.

steps.title: Capture and specify (code kinds)
steps.text: Starts a work, writes REQUIREMENTS.md and the technical specification. It asks at most one question. Which extra spec sections appear depends on the kind: an api adds API contracts, a data-model adds a migration plan.

steps.title: Detail the tasks (code kinds)
steps.text: Writes task files that depend on the kind. An api gets three tasks: model, handler, integration test. A ui or cli gets a build task and a test task. A config gets one task.

steps.title: Grading gate (code kinds)
steps.text: An independent reviewer grades the documents until they reach the minimum grade (A+ by default for shortcuts), or it stops after 3 rounds with no improvement.

steps.title: Approval stop
steps.text: Stops with nothing built. You run /aid-execute when ready.

steps.title: Knowledge Base and document kinds
steps.text: roadmap, backlog, mvp, architecture, stack, testing-strategy and cicd turn a ready design from /aid-design into the matching document under .aid/knowledge/. document and diagram write a draft, show it with a proposed location, and place it only after you approve.

writes: A new work folder .aid/works/work-NNN-<short-name>/ with REQUIREMENTS.md, tasks/task-NNN/DETAIL.md files and STATE.yml, inside its own git worktree (a separate checkout on a branch named work-NNN). (code kinds)
The matching document under .aid/knowledge/ and a settings entry, for the Knowledge Base kinds. The design file in .aid/design/ is used up once it is turned into the document.
A document or diagram at a location you approve, for the document and diagram kinds. These never write to .aid/knowledge/.
aid-create.gate: Code kinds: you approve the plan by running /aid-execute. Document and diagram kinds: you approve the draft and where it goes.
notes: api, ui, theme, cli, data-model, data-pipeline, messaging, integration, job, config, infra, test and dashboard run the planning steps. roadmap, backlog, mvp, architecture, stack, testing-strategy, cicd, document and diagram follow their own reference file instead.
The Knowledge Base kinds refuse to run while the design still lists open questions, unless you add --override-open-questions. They write the document, then show it to you, so use git to undo.
With no kind, it plans a generic code change as a single build task.

aid-create-ticket.summary: Files one new ticket in your issue tracker after showing you exactly what will be sent.
aid-create-ticket.when: Use it when work must be recorded where your team tracks it. Nothing is sent until you confirm.
aid-create-ticket.example: /aid-create-ticket --level story --parent PROJ-12 "Add pagination to the /orders list"

steps.title: Read the request
steps.text: Flags --connector, --level and --parent can come in any order; the rest of the line is the description.

steps.title: Find the tracker
steps.text: It uses the matching connector, asks if several fit, or falls back to your tool's own tracker.

steps.title: Draft
steps.text: A title, level and parent are worked out. Nothing is chosen silently.

steps.title: Match the level
steps.text: It reads the tracker's real issue types and maps epic, story or task to the closest one.

steps.title: You confirm
steps.text: You see the exact payload and choose File it, Edit or Cancel; if the level is unknown you pick it here.

steps.title: File and report
steps.text: The ticket is created, a parent link is added if possible, and you get the new reference.

writes: Nothing in your project files.
One new ticket in the tracker, only after you choose File it.
aid-create-ticket.gate: You confirm the exact ticket (and pick its level if it was not clear) before it is filed.
notes: The parent must be on the same tracker as the new ticket.
If the tracker has no matching type, the ticket is filed as a plain issue and says so in the preview.
Without any text it prints usage and stops.
Works with a connector of type mcp tagged issue-tracker, or your tool's own tracker integration.

aid-define.summary: Splits the approved requirements into features and checks them against the Knowledge Base and the code.
aid-define.when: Use it right after the requirements are approved. If the requirements themselves need to change, go back to /aid-describe.

steps.title: Check approval
steps.text: If the requirements are not approved yet, it stops and sends you to /aid-describe.

steps.title: Propose features
steps.text: An architect agent proposes a list of features from the functional requirements; you approve it or ask for changes until it is right.

steps.title: Write the features
steps.text: Each approved feature gets its own section in REQUIREMENTS.md.

steps.title: Cross-check
steps.text: A reviewer agent checks the requirements and features against the Knowledge Base and codebase and grades them.

steps.title: Resolve gaps
steps.text: Each finding becomes a question that you answer one at a time.

steps.title: Close or reopen
steps.text: You can add information, run the cross-check again, or finish.

writes: `.aid/works/work-NNN-*/REQUIREMENTS.md`: one feature section per feature.
`.aid/works/work-NNN-*/STATE.yml`: the feature list and any new questions.
aid-define.gate: You approve the feature list, and answer the questions the cross-check raises.
notes: --features work-NNN redoes the feature split even if features exist.
Changes to the requirements themselves belong in /aid-describe.
Does not run in Plan mode.

aid-deploy.summary: Verifies the build, packages completed deliveries into a release and writes the release notes.
aid-deploy.when: Use it when deliveries are complete and graded. How the release is produced comes from your Knowledge Base, so it fits PRs, containers, packages and more.

steps.title: Assess
steps.text: It checks which deliveries are complete and not yet shipped, and how your project packages releases; if unknown, it asks you.

steps.title: Choose deliveries
steps.text: You pick which ready deliveries go in this release, plus a version tag and a package name.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: A full build, the full test suite and lint all run on the combined scope.

steps.title: Decide on failures
steps.text: If anything fails you choose: fix small things here, or go back to /aid-execute.

steps.title: Package
steps.text: It produces what your project calls for, such as a pull request, image, or published package.

steps.title: Release notes and wrap up
steps.text: Notes are written into the package file, Knowledge Base changes are queued as questions, and deliveries are marked Shipped.

writes: `.aid/works/work-NNN-*/packages/package-NNN-<name>.md`: verification, deployment record and release notes.
The work's `STATE.yml`: deploy status and Shipped marks.
Whatever your packaging produces (PR, image, published package).
`.aid/knowledge/STATE.md`: pending questions for Knowledge Base changes it spots.
aid-deploy.gate: You choose the deliveries to include, and decide what to do when verification fails.
notes: It never edits Knowledge Base documents directly; it queues questions for /aid-discover.
If you give a free-form description instead of a work, it sets up a small work and stops for approval without shipping anything.
Use /aid-ask or /aid-config first if packaging details are missing from the Knowledge Base.

aid-deprecate.summary: Plan a deprecation: mark something as going away and point callers to the replacement. Nothing is deleted.
aid-deprecate.when: Use it when callers need time to move. When the time comes to delete, use /aid-remove.
aid-deprecate.example: /aid-deprecate the v1 /orders endpoint, replaced by /v2/orders, removal planned for the next major version

steps.title: Start a work
steps.text: Checks whether other works exist. If they do, it asks whether this is a new work or a continuation of one. For a new work it creates a separate git worktree and a work folder, so your main branch stays untouched.

steps.title: Capture
steps.text: Writes REQUIREMENTS.md with the target, its replacement and how to move to it, and when it is expected to go away. It asks at most one question, if the target or the replacement is unclear.

steps.title: Specify and plan
steps.text: Adds the technical specification to REQUIREMENTS.md, section 11. There is one feature and one delivery, so there is nothing to sequence and no separate plan file.

steps.title: Detail the tasks
steps.text: Usually one task: add the deprecation warning in the form your project uses (an annotation, a log warning or a docs banner) and write the migration note that points to the replacement.

steps.title: Grading gate
steps.text: An independent reviewer grades the requirements, then the task files. Anything below the minimum grade goes back to be fixed and is reviewed again. The default minimum for these shortcuts is A+, and you can lower it in settings. After 3 rounds with no improvement it stops and writes an IMPEDIMENT file.

steps.title: Approval stop
steps.text: Prints the work and its grades, then stops. Nothing has been built. You read the documents, then run /aid-execute yourself when you are happy.

writes: A new work folder .aid/works/work-NNN-<short-name>/ with REQUIREMENTS.md, tasks/task-NNN/DETAIL.md files and STATE.yml, inside its own git worktree (a separate checkout on a branch named work-NNN).
Nothing in your source code is touched. Code changes only happen later, in /aid-execute.
aid-deprecate.gate: You read REQUIREMENTS.md and the task files, then decide whether to run /aid-execute. The shortcut never starts building on its own.
notes: It only plans. Nothing is built until you run /aid-execute.
Each run starts a new work. To carry on with a halted one, run /aid-execute on it.
The deprecated thing keeps working. Removing it later is a separate /aid-remove.

aid-describe.summary: Interviews you one question at a time and writes REQUIREMENTS.md, the approved description of what to build.
aid-describe.when: Use it to start a new piece of work when the scope, users and acceptance criteria are not pinned down. For one small, clear change try /aid-triage.

steps.title: Start or resume a work
steps.text: It asks for a short name, creates an isolated git worktree and the work folder; if works exist, it asks whether this is new or a continuation.

steps.title: Interview
steps.text: It asks one question per turn and updates REQUIREMENTS.md after each answer.

steps.title: Answer questions from later steps
steps.text: Questions that later skills left in the work are asked first when you come back.

steps.title: Seed the Knowledge Base
steps.text: On an empty project it also drafts starting Knowledge Base documents, checks them for conflicts and has them reviewed.

steps.title: Fill the Knowledge Base
steps.text: Facts you gave are written into Knowledge Base documents; it may ask a few extra questions and you can say skip.

steps.title: Confirm name and summary
steps.text: You confirm the work name and one-sentence description, then read a summary of the requirements.

steps.title: You approve
steps.text: You approve, or add something and the interview continues.

writes: `.aid/works/work-NNN-*/REQUIREMENTS.md`.
`.aid/works/work-NNN-*/STATE.yml`: interview progress and questions.
A git worktree and branch for the work.
Knowledge Base documents under `.aid/knowledge/` that the interview filled in.
aid-describe.gate: You approve the requirements. Nothing moves to /aid-define until you do.
notes: Needs the `.aid/` folder; run /aid-config first if it says the workspace is missing.
It always asks before continuing an existing work, even if only one exists.
--reset work-NNN deletes that work folder and starts over.
If a tracker connector is set up, after approval it suggests filing an epic with /aid-create-ticket. It never does it by itself.
Does not run in Plan mode.

aid-design.summary: Design something to be kept and later built: an API, UI, data model, architecture, roadmap and more.
aid-design.when: Use it while the shape is still open and you want it written down. To test an idea with a throwaway model use /aid-prototype; to build it use /aid-create.
aid-design.example: /aid-design api public orders API for the mobile app

steps.title: Intake
steps.text: Asks what to design if you gave no subject. Starts a work and a separate git worktree. Reads an earlier design on the same subject, so running it again improves the design instead of starting over.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: An architect agent writes the design, based on your Knowledge Base and code, including accessibility notes. With a kind, it writes a design note in .aid/design/. With no kind, it writes DESIGN.md in the work folder.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: A clean-context reviewer checks that the design is grounded, complete, consistent and buildable. It is reworked until clean, or stops after 3 rounds.

steps.title: Present
steps.text: Shows the design and stops. You decide whether and when to build it.

steps.title: Hand off
steps.text: Prints suggestions, such as /aid-create or /aid-update to build it. It never starts them.

writes: With a kind: a design note at .aid/design/<kind>.md.
With no kind: DESIGN.md in the work folder .aid/works/work-NNN-<short-name>/.
Never your source code and never the Knowledge Base.
aid-design.gate: You decide whether the design is ready and when to build it.
notes: Every kind follows the same steps; the kind decides which design note it writes and what that note must settle.
A later /aid-create for the Knowledge Base kinds refuses while the note still lists open questions.

aid-detail.summary: Breaks each delivery into small, typed tasks in dependency order, ready for one agent session each.
aid-detail.when: Use it after the plan is approved. It only slices what the plan and specs already decided; it makes no new design choices.

steps.title: Check the plan
steps.text: If PLAN.md is missing, it stops and sends you to /aid-plan.

steps.title: Propose tasks
steps.text: For the first delivery an architect agent proposes small tasks, each with a type, scope and acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Discuss
steps.text: You adjust the tasks until they look right.

steps.title: Write and repeat
steps.text: Task files are written, then the same loop runs for the next delivery.

steps.title: Build the execution graph
steps.text: Which tasks wait on which, and which can run in parallel, is written to PLAN.md.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: A reviewer grades the whole task list against the plan and specs.

writes: `.aid/works/work-NNN-*/deliveries/delivery-NNN/tasks/task-NNN/DETAIL.md`: the task definition.
`.aid/works/work-NNN-*/deliveries/delivery-NNN/tasks/task-NNN/STATE.yml`: the task starts as Pending.
`.aid/works/work-NNN-*/PLAN.md`: the execution graph.
aid-detail.gate: You agree on the tasks for each delivery.
notes: Every task must fit one agent session and be one reviewable unit.
Tasks are numbered across the whole work, not per delivery.
--reset clears the tasks folder.
Does not run in Plan mode.

aid-discover.summary: Reads your existing code and builds the Knowledge Base: architecture, conventions and patterns, graded and approved by you.
aid-discover.when: Use it when the project already has code and no Knowledge Base yet. For an empty project there is nothing to read, so go to /aid-describe.

steps.title: Ask about outside sources and tools
steps.text: You can list docs, specs and tools (like an issue tracker) to include; you can skip both.

steps.title: Scan and write
steps.text: Helper agents read the project in parallel and write the Knowledge Base documents. An empty project stops here and points you to /aid-describe.

steps.title: Grade
steps.text: A reviewer grades every document for accuracy and evidence.

steps.title: Answer open questions
steps.text: Anything the agents could not prove from the code becomes a question; it answers what it can confirm and asks you the rest.

steps.title: Fix
steps.text: Documents are corrected and graded again until the grade reaches your minimum.

steps.title: You approve
steps.text: You read the Knowledge Base and approve it or add a consideration.

writes: `.aid/knowledge/*.md`: the Knowledge Base documents plus `INDEX.md` and `README.md`.
`.aid/knowledge/STATE.md`: grade, open questions and review history.
`.aid/connectors/`: only if you add tools in the first step.
`.aid/settings.yml`: the knowledge block (branch and date of the last build).
aid-discover.gate: You approve the Knowledge Base once it meets the minimum grade and no questions are left.
notes: Each run goes as far as it can and stops when it needs you. Run it again to continue.
The minimum grade defaults to A. Use --grade to change it; --reset deletes everything in `.aid/knowledge/` and starts over.
It is built not to guess: unclear points are asked, not written down as fact.
Long steps can take many minutes; it prints progress while helper agents run.
Does not run in Plan mode, because helper agents need to write.

aid-document.summary: Write a document now: a how-to, reference, decision record, runbook, tutorial or similar, and place it where you approve.
aid-document.when: Use it for documentation about something. For project knowledge in .aid/knowledge/ use /aid-update-kb; for a design use /aid-design.
aid-document.example: /aid-document runbook what to do when the nightly import job fails

steps.title: Intake
steps.text: Asks what to document and for whom, if you gave none. Works out the format and the kind of document from your request. Starts a work and a separate git worktree. Reads a design note in .aid/design/document.md if there is one.

steps.title: Author
steps.text: A tech writer agent drafts the document in the work folder, checked against your Knowledge Base and code.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: A clean-context reviewer checks accuracy and that the right parts for that kind of document are there. It is reworked until clean, or stops after 3 rounds.

steps.title: Present
steps.text: Shows the draft and the place it proposes to put it, and stops for your approval.

steps.title: Place (only if you approve)
steps.text: Writes the document to the approved location. For an existing file it shows a diff and never overwrites silently. If you decline, the draft stays in the work folder.

writes: A draft in the work folder .aid/works/work-NNN-<short-name>/.
The final document at the location you approve, such as docs/, a decision-records folder or CHANGELOG.md.
Never .aid/knowledge/.
aid-document.gate: You approve the draft and where it is placed.
notes: With no kind, it writes a general how-to, reference, explanation or status report in markdown.
It is the same as /aid-create document with the kind preselected.

aid-execute.summary: Carries out a planned task by its type, checks it, and runs a graded quality gate when the whole delivery is done.
aid-execute.when: Use it when a delivery's tasks are detailed. Run it per task, in the order of the execution graph. For a small one-off fix, use /aid-fix instead.

steps.title: Check the task
steps.text: It finds the task, confirms that tasks it depends on are Done and the working tree is clean, and switches to the delivery branch.

steps.title: Do the work
steps.text: An agent suited to the task type (research, design, implement, test, document, migrate, refactor, configure) does only what the task's scope says.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.text: A small reviewer looks for serious problems; critical ones are fixed on the spot and high ones are noted for the delivery gate.

steps.title: Mark done
steps.text: The task is marked Done. Asking for a Done task again asks whether you want to reopen it.

steps.title: Delivery gate
steps.text: When every task in a delivery is Done, a full review grades the whole delivery and code issues are fixed and graded again until it meets the minimum.

steps.title: Stop when blocked
steps.text: If it cannot continue it marks the task Failed and writes an impediment note with options.

writes: The task's output: code, tests, docs, configs or research, committed on branch `aid/work-NNN-delivery-NNN`.
The task's `STATE.yml`, and the delivery's `STATE.yml` (progress, review history, gate grade).
`.aid/works/work-NNN-*/delivery-NNN-issues.md`: high issues deferred to the gate.
`.aid/works/work-NNN-*/IMPEDIMENT-task-NNN.md` when it is blocked.
aid-execute.gate: At the delivery gate you see every issue listed; problems that are not code (the task, the spec or the Knowledge Base) pause the run until you fix them upstream.
notes: One branch per delivery; all its tasks share it.
The per-task check is a quick one. The full graded review happens once per delivery.
The delivery gate stops with a warning if the grade does not improve after three rounds.
Giving a delivery instead of a task (for example delivery-005) runs its tasks in parallel where the graph allows; on hosts without background agents it falls back to one at a time.
Does not run in Plan mode.

aid-experiment.summary: Plan a controlled experiment or A/B test, with the success bar fixed before anything runs.
aid-experiment.when: Use it to test a hypothesis with variants and a metric. For a one-time look at data you already have use /aid-report; to try an idea cheaply use /aid-prototype.
aid-experiment.example: /aid-experiment does a shorter checkout form raise completed orders by 5 percent

steps.title: Start a work
steps.text: Checks whether other works exist. If they do, it asks whether this is a new work or a continuation of one. For a new work it creates a separate git worktree and a work folder, so your main branch stays untouched.

steps.title: Capture
steps.text: Writes REQUIREMENTS.md with the hypothesis, at least two variants, the success metric, the significance bar, sample size, guardrail metrics, duration or stopping rule, and the audience. These are fixed in the acceptance criteria before any run, so the result cannot be judged against a bar chosen afterward. It asks at most one question.

steps.title: Specify and plan
steps.text: Adds the technical specification to REQUIREMENTS.md, section 11, including an experiment design section: how groups are assigned, how metrics are computed and which statistical method is used. There is one feature and one delivery, so there is nothing to sequence and no separate plan file.

steps.title: Detail the tasks
steps.text: Writes a chain of tasks. Task 1 designs the experiment. An optional task builds the variants, only if your description says they must be built. The last task runs the experiment, checks the result against the bar and ends with a recommendation.

steps.title: Grading gate
steps.text: An independent reviewer grades the requirements, then the task files. Anything below the minimum grade goes back to be fixed and is reviewed again. The default minimum for these shortcuts is A+, and you can lower it in settings. After 3 rounds with no improvement it stops and writes an IMPEDIMENT file.

steps.title: Approval stop
steps.text: Prints the work and its grades, then stops. Nothing has been built. You read the documents, then run /aid-execute yourself when you are happy.

writes: A new work folder .aid/works/work-NNN-<short-name>/ with REQUIREMENTS.md, tasks/task-NNN/DETAIL.md files and STATE.yml, inside its own git worktree (a separate checkout on a branch named work-NNN).
Nothing in your source code is touched. Code changes only happen later, in /aid-execute.
aid-experiment.gate: You read REQUIREMENTS.md and the task files, then decide whether to run /aid-execute. The shortcut never starts building on its own.
notes: It only plans. Nothing is built until you run /aid-execute.
Each run starts a new work. To carry on with a halted one, run /aid-execute on it.
Analysis of data you already have, with no controlled variants, is /aid-report.

aid-fix.summary: Plan the fix for a bug, regression, incident or vulnerability, with a test that proves it is closed.
aid-fix.when: Use it when something is wrong and you can describe how to see it. For new behavior use /aid-update; for cleanup with no bug use /aid-refactor; to find problems first use /aid-review or /aid-test.
aid-fix.example: /aid-fix the login form rejects passwords containing a plus sign

steps.title: Start a work
steps.text: Checks whether other works exist. If they do, it asks whether this is a new work or a continuation of one. For a new work it creates a separate git worktree and a work folder, so your main branch stays untouched.

steps.title: Capture
steps.text: Writes REQUIREMENTS.md with the symptom, the steps to reproduce, expected versus actual behavior and the affected area. It also notes whether this is a defect, a regression, an incident or a vulnerability, guessed from your wording. It asks at most one question, usually when the reproduction steps are missing.

steps.text: The connector's file is removed.

steps.title: Refresh the index
steps.text: `INDEX.md` is rebuilt without that tool; other connectors are untouched.

writes: Deletes `.aid/connectors/<tool>.md` and `.aid/connectors/.secrets/<tool>`.
`.aid/connectors/INDEX.md` (rebuilt).
notes: It does not ask for confirmation before deleting.
Safe to run twice: on a tool that is already gone it does nothing and succeeds.
It does not touch your tool's own configuration in your editor.
Does not run in Plan mode.

aid-update.summary: Plan a change to something that exists: code such as an API or job, a project document in the Knowledge Base, or a document.
aid-update.when: Use it when behavior or content should change on purpose. For a defect use /aid-fix; for cleanup that keeps behavior the same use /aid-refactor.
aid-update.example: /aid-update api add a status filter to GET /orders

steps.title: Pick the route
steps.text: The first word can be a kind. Code kinds run the planning steps below. roadmap, mvp, backlog, architecture, stack, testing-strategy, cicd and document follow their own path.

steps.title: Capture the delta (code kinds)
steps.text: Starts a work and writes REQUIREMENTS.md with what the thing does today, what it should do after, and the new acceptance criteria. It asks at most one question.

steps.title: Specify and detail (code kinds)
steps.text: Adds the technical specification and task files. The tasks are the same ones /aid-create would write for that kind, but each is limited to the change.

steps.title: Grading gate (code kinds)
steps.text: An independent reviewer grades the documents until they reach the minimum grade (A+ by default for shortcuts), or it stops after 3 rounds with no improvement.

steps.title: Approval stop
steps.text: Stops with nothing built. You run /aid-execute when ready.

steps.title: Knowledge Base and document kinds
steps.text: Edits only the part of the document it owns, shows the result, and leaves the rest of the file unchanged. For document it also shows a diff before writing.

writes: A new work folder .aid/works/work-NNN-<short-name>/ with REQUIREMENTS.md, tasks/task-NNN/DETAIL.md files and STATE.yml, inside its own git worktree (a separate checkout on a branch named work-NNN). (code kinds)
The matching document under .aid/knowledge/, for the Knowledge Base kinds. A design file in .aid/design/ is read first and used up if there is one.
The edited document at its existing location, for the document kind. It never writes to .aid/knowledge/.
aid-update.gate: Code kinds: you approve the plan by running /aid-execute. Document kind: you approve the diff.
notes: api, ui, theme, cli, data-model, data-pipeline, messaging, integration, job, config, infra, test and dashboard run the planning steps. The rest follow their own reference file.
update has no diagram kind; use /aid-update document.
The Knowledge Base kinds change the file before they show it to you, so use git to undo.

aid-update-kb.summary: Applies one targeted, human-confirmed change to the Knowledge Base, in its own worktree.
aid-update-kb.when: Use it when a specific fact changed and you want that edit and nothing more. For a broad sweep of drift, use /aid-housekeep.
aid-update-kb.example: /aid-update-kb the payments service now retries 3 times instead of 5

steps.title: Set up a safe copy
steps.text: It makes its own worktree and branch `aid/update-kb-<timestamp>` so your tree is untouched.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.text: A clean-context agent works out how your instruction lands in the Knowledge Base.

steps.title: Plan the scope
steps.text: It lists exactly which documents and passages it would change.

steps.title: You confirm the scope
steps.text: Confirm, adjust or cancel before any edit exists.

steps.title: Apply and review
steps.text: Only the confirmed changes are made, then reviewed and fixed until the grade meets the minimum.

steps.title: You approve the edits
steps.text: You approve the actual changes.

steps.title: Commit
steps.text: The change is checked once more and committed on the branch.

writes: The Knowledge Base documents in `.aid/knowledge/` that you confirmed, inside the new worktree.
One commit on branch `aid/update-kb-<timestamp>`.
A temporary run file in `.aid/.temp/`, removed when done.
aid-update-kb.gate: Two stops: you confirm the scope before any edit, and approve the edits before the commit.
notes: Without a prompt it prints usage and stops.
Running it again with the same text resumes the paused run; different text starts a separate one.
The worktree is created from the branch named master. It stops rather than work in your own tree if it cannot make the worktree.

aid-update-ticket.summary: Changes one part of a ticket (description, comment or status) after you confirm the exact change.
aid-update-ticket.when: Use it to update a ticket in your tracker. It changes only the part you name, so use it for one change at a time.

steps.title: Check the request
steps.text: The first word must be description, comment or status; anything else prints usage and stops.

steps.title: Find the connector
steps.text: A `jira:` prefix picks it directly; otherwise it uses the one catalogued tracker or asks.

steps.title: Load what it needs
steps.text: For a status change it fetches the allowed next states; for a description it fetches the current text; a comment needs nothing.

steps.title: Prepare the change
steps.text: A description replaces the old one, a comment is added, a status is set. A status that is not allowed lists the valid ones and stops.

steps.title: You confirm
steps.text: You see the exact change (before and after for a description) and choose to go ahead, edit or cancel.

steps.title: Write
steps.text: One call is made to the tracker and the result is reported.

writes: Nothing in your project files.
One change to the ticket in the tracker, only after you confirm.
aid-update-ticket.gate: You confirm the exact change before it is sent.
notes: The part is the first word, then the ticket reference, then the new content.
If the tracker cannot list valid statuses, the change is tried anyway and its error shown if it is rejected.
The confirm prompt reuses the same buttons as ticket creation, and the first one is labeled File it even when you are updating.
Everything after the ticket reference is used as typed.
